title: Terraform module: VPC security controls (SG/NACL/Private DNS/egress)
creator: Priya Singh
description: Develop a reusable Terraform module (aws and gcp variants) that implements Redwood-standard VPC security controls for Private deployments. The module will own: security groups (stateful, minimal defaults), network ACLs (stateless layer), private DNS (Route53 private hosted zone + resolver rules), and a configurable egress policy (whitelist-first with optional default-deny). The module must be composable for Dedicated and Private stacks, support zero-downtime security group rollouts, and include automated tests (terratest/integration) plus CI gates (plan approvals, tfsec, checkov). Deliverables: tf module code, examples for a 3-subnet (public/private/management) layout, upgrade/migration docs, health-check lambdas and alerting runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables for allowed_ingress_cidrs, management_cidrs, allowed_egress_destinations, egress_filter_mode (whitelist|blacklist), enable_flow_logs, and private_dns_zone_name

Default behaviour is: deny all ingress; allow management CIDR and internal ALB/subnet ranges; deny all egress except explicit allowlist (recommended list includes SSM, CloudWatch, ECR, Redwood control plane endpoints)
Provides outputs: security_group_ids, network_acl_ids, private_zone_id, resolver_endpoint_ids
Zero-downtime SG upgrades: documented pattern and helper that creates new SGs, attaches to ENIs, then detaches old SGs
Integration tests validate: DNS resolution against private zone, egress allowlist connectivity checks, NACL ordering effects, and terraform plan diffs are reviewed
CI enforces tfsec and manual approval step for any change that widens egress or opens 0.0.0.0/0 outbound
Module supports tagging and KMS key for Flow Logs encryption
Security review completed and signed-off in Confluence before merge
implementation_notes: Module layout will follow terraform registry conventions: modules/vpc-security/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf,README.md}. Provide two providers aliases (aws.primary, aws.peer) for cross-account resolver endpoints. Use aws_security_group for stateful controls and aws_network_acl for subnet-level hardening; NACL rule numbering will follow reserved ranges: 100-199 for system, 200-299 customer. Egress policies implemented via both SG egress and an explicit egress proxy/egress NACL depending on egress_filter_mode. Add optional aws_vpc_endpoint resources for S3/ECR to avoid public egress when allowlist is used. Include a small lambda (python) deployed via module optional flag that runs synthetic egress checks every 5m and emits CloudWatch metrics and paging alerts on failure.
upgrade_plan: Follow semver for module versions. Migration steps for widening to new SGs: (1) bump module version in terragrunt stack and plan in Canary account/subnet, (2) module will create new security_group resources with suffix _v2, (3) automation (or operator) will attach new SG IDs to target ENIs via aws_network_interface_attachment resource pattern or via AWS SDK script (module provides helper script), (4) once metrics/health checks stable for 30m, destroy old SG resources. For NACL changes, apply in two-step: lower-risk rules staged with higher rule numbers, monitor flow logs, then promote rule numbers to production ordering. Provide a migration script in scripts/upgrade-sg.sh and a terraform state move recipe in README.
testing_plan: Unit tests: terraform validate and tflint. Static analysis: tfsec and checkov rules17 and rules for egress. Integration tests: terratest suite covers VPC creation, private hosted zone attach, resolver rules, egress synthetic probe (lambda), and attachment/detach SG lifecycle. Test matrix: aws-us-east-1 small account (canary), aws-eu-west-1, and mocked GCP VPC variant. CI pipeline: PR -> plan -> tfsec -> terratest in parallel -> manual security approval for any egress widenings -> apply on merge to staging followed by canary promotion.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Introducing an overly-restrictive default deny could break control-plane agents (SSM/ECR). Mitigation: default allowlist includes SSM, ECR, CloudWatch, Control-plane endpoints; module has an allow_management_cidrs bool to open management CIDRs during onboarding
Risk: NACL order bugs cause accidental traffic block. Mitigation: reserve rule number ranges and provide unit tests verifying expected permit/deny for canonical flows
Risk: DNS misconfiguration causing service discovery failures. Mitigation: resolver rules, cross-account resolver endpoints, and automated DNS resolution health checks; rollbacks via canary stack
Risk: Operator error during SG swap. Mitigation: helper scripts + guidance, and automation in the module for safe replace with attach/verify/detach pattern
notes_and_decisions: 2026-03-11 - Decision: default policy will be whitelist-first (deny-all-everything unless allowed). Rationale: Private deployments often host sensitive customer data and explicit egress control reduces exfil risk. (Decision by Priya, Avery, and Diego)

2026-03-11 - Trade-off: Implementing both SG and NACL increases complexity but gives defense-in-depth. We will document both layers and recommend SGs as primary管理 control; NACLs reserved for broad emergency blocks.

2026-03-12 - Implementation detail: choose to surface 'egress_ping_checks' variable enabling lambda-based health checks vs relying purely on Route53 health checks because we need TCP+HTTP egress validation. (Avery)
2026-03-12 - Security review: initial review scheduled for 2026-03-15; reviewers: Diego Martinez, Liam O'Connor, Samantha Reed
